text:
alicia: heads-up — seeing repeated allocator-driven preemptions in eu-west dedicated pool this morning. tenants on small slices getting bounced and p99 latency for interactive jobs spikes.

raj: any obvious correlation? recent config rollouts?

alicia: looks related to bursts hitting egress and NVMe IO at the same time. allocator logs show sustained backpressure and fast slot retries.

```
allocator: backpressure=0.82 retries=7 preemptions=21
host: nvme_write_q=95% wait_ms=14
scheduler: warm_hold=6s
```

marco: also seeing kvcache regen when slots flip — that plus egress congestion is amplifying tail. small noisy tenants repeatedly reclaim warm slots.

jen: we rolled `burst-align-v2` last night in eu-west and us-east. I suspected it might tighten preemption thresholds.

alicia: confirmed — rollout timestamp 2025-11-02T03:12Z per deploy logs.

ops-bot: deploy: burst-align-v2 rolled to eu-west at 2025-11-02T03:12Z by canary pipeline :gear:

raj: short-term mitigation suggestions:
- apply per-tenant egress token-bucket on host NICs (limit burst window)
- increase scheduler warm_hold to reduce slot churn
Both reduce preemptions but change unit economics (more idle warm slots) and risk queuing for heavy embedding tenants.

marco: +1 to warm_hold change first. Throttling egress is effective but could hurt throughput for sustained workloads.

jen: can we canary both in a single AZ? e.g., extend warm_hold to 20s in eu-west-1a, and enable NIC-level egress TB with conservative params on the same hosts.

alicia: plan: canary group = eu-west-1a, 12 hosts. I'll own monitoring and rollback. assign @raj TB config, @marco scheduler patch, @jen approval for rollout window.

raj: TB config I'll push (host-level):
```
# egress token bucket
net.egress_token_rate=800mbps
net.egress_burst_bytes=10485760  # 10MB
```
Pushing gradual apply via fleet config to avoid simultaneous spikes.

marco: scheduler patch: `warm_hold_secs=20` ready, testing now in staging.

ops-bot: alert: detected preemption-rate increase in eu-west-1b post-rollout. Rate x1.7 baseline. Engineers notified.

jen: keep the canary run for 2 hours, gather metrics: preemptions/min, p99 latency, avg slot utilization, egress tail.

alicia: will post graphs in ~2h. immediate goal: reduce preemptions by >=40% with <15% warm-slot cost increase. if positive, stage roll with phased AZs.

sre-oncall: ack — will watch paging thresholds and slow-roll in case of regressions.

raj: FYI — if TB causes request queuing we might need a fallback: mark noisy tenants for dedicated mini-pools or apply per-tenant egress credits to preserve SLO.

marco: agreed. long-term we should consider fractional dedicated carveouts for consistently noisy tenants; cheaper than churn-driven retries.

alicia: returning with initial metrics in 2hrs. tagging infra-leads for visibility. :mag:

jen: thanks. please include cost delta estimate and a brief runbook for rollback in the canary notes.
